wages.text: She said she supports raising the federal minimum wage.
wages.quote: I do support raising the federal minimum wage, and I think that is important for allowing families who are working to be able to take care of their own.

debt.text: She supports raising Social Security taxes on earnings above $400,000 to strengthen the program’s solvency and security.
debt.quote: I believe that we need to implement the Social Security tax for those earning higher than $400,000 to help increase the solvency and ensure the stability of the program.

housing.text: She proposes cutting outdated red tape and zoning rules that slow affordable housing construction.
housing.quote: Making it easier to build affordable housing by cutting outdated red tape and zoning rules that slow down projects and drive up prices.

immigration.text: She supports expanding citizenship pathways and focusing immigration enforcement on criminals and traffickers.
immigration.quote: That means expanding pathways to citizenship, faster legal processing, and enforcement focused where it belongs: on criminals and traffickers, not on our neighbors.

guns.text: She supports universal background checks, closing sales loopholes, and grants for state red-flag laws.
guns.quote: Passing Universal background checks to protect lawful gun owners while stopping criminals

health.text: She supports a public insurance option open to everyone and expanding Medicare coverage.
health.quote: Allowing everyone to opt in to a public insurance option, regardless of age, expanding coverage, and driving down costs across the marketplace.

energy.text: She supports investing in clean energy and describes climate change as a national security crisis.
energy.quote: Investing in clean energy, expanding federal investments in solar, wind, and geothermal projects.

voting.text: She called the SAVE Act a voter suppression tool and criticized efforts to interfere with mail-in voting.
voting.quote: the SAVE Act is just another voter suppression tool. I say this as an election security expert

tax.text: Lawler backed tax cuts for families and seniors and described his work as delivering tax relief.
tax.quote: Congressman Mike Lawler has delivered significant tax relief for Hudson Valley's working families, seniors, and small businesses.

wages.text: He voted for legislation accelerating first collective-bargaining contracts and said organized workers deserve a meaningful workplace voice.
wages.quote: Workers who choose to organize deserve a fair shot at reaching their first contract.

trade.text: Lawler said he viewed Trump's tariffs as an effective short-term negotiating tool while urging faster trade agreements.
trade.quote: he believes Trump’s tariffs are an effective negotiating tool in the short-term.

debt.text: He has said he opposes cuts to Social Security and Medicare and supported legislation expanding some Social Security benefits.
debt.quote: I have opposed any cuts to Social Security and Medicare and will continue to oppose any policy that comes forward that would cut these essential programs.

housing.text: He has introduced and supported legislation intended to increase housing supply, streamline development, and lower costs.
housing.quote: Mike Lawler has championed tax relief for homeowners and introduced and authored multiple bills that became law to increase housing supply and lower costs

schools.text: He cosponsored legislation offering parents tax credits for a range of school options, including private and religious schools.
schools.quote: Cosponsored the Educational Choice for Children Act (H.R. 833) to give parents access to the best educational options for their child - public, private, charter, homeschooling, or religious

safety.text: He requested federal funding for sheriff’s office equipment and public safety training facilities.
safety.quote: The funding would be used for necessary law enforcement priorities such as police vehicles, equipment to be utilized at a new reality-based public safety training facility, and the structural analysis and design of the facility.

immigration.text: Lawler supports a secure border and continued deportations while also backing legal status, not citizenship, for long-term undocumented immigrants without criminal records.
immigration.quote: Along with building on Mr. Trump’s border policies, a realistic plan would provide a path to legal status — not citizenship — for long-term illegal immigrants without criminal records.

guns.text: He cosponsored a bill to strengthen background-check requirements.
guns.quote: Cosponsored the Bipartisan Background Checks Act (H.R. 18) to strengthen existing background check requirements

abortion.text: He opposes a federal abortion ban but supports restrictions including limits on late-term abortions and parental notification for minors.
abortion.quote: Opposes a federal ban on abortion, and would never force a rape victim or woman facing a serious health issue to continue a pregnancy against their will

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: Lawler says transgender women should not participate in women's sports or use women's spaces.
gender.quote: Biological males should not be allowed to participate in women's sports or occupy biological women's spaces whether it be bathrooms, locker rooms, sorority houses, women's shelters, or prison.

cannabis.text: He opposed rescheduling marijuana and argued that it is a gateway drug leading some users to harder substances.
cannabis.quote: But I think rescheduling marijuana is wrong. The fact is, marijuana is a gateway drug. Most of the people [who] end up using harder substances start out on marijuana.

health.text: He supported extending Affordable Care Act subsidies and funding care for Medicare, Medicaid, and uninsured patients.
health.quote: Took on his own party leadership to force a House vote on extending Affordable Care Act subsidies and prevent premium increases for millions of Americans

energy.text: He supports an all-of-the-above energy strategy emphasizing affordability and reliability, alongside some environmental protections.
energy.quote: My approach is straightforward: lower utility costs for working and middle-class families, strengthen grid reliability, promote American energy independence, and protect the clean air, clean water, and natural beauty that make the Hudson Valley such a great place to live.

voting.text: Lawler supports requiring photo identification for voting and voted for the SAVE Act.
voting.quote: It’s a simple way to ensure that people voting are who they say they are, and if you need a photo ID to buy alcohol or cigarettes, why not for voting?
